seo.metaDescription: Using tally-charts in React Server Components: what renders on the server, when a file needs 'use client', and what to import from tally-charts/core.

props.markdown: The charts work in the Next.js App Router and any other framework with React Server Components. The rule is small: a chart is a client component, so everything you give it has to be able to cross from the server to the browser. Plain data does, functions do not.

props.text: Rendering a chart from a server file

props.markdown: The main entry `tally-charts` starts with `'use client'`. Importing `<Chart>`, `BarChart` or `ZoneMeter` from it in a Server Component file is fine, because the entry already marks the boundary. The server renders the SVG into the HTML and the browser hydrates it for hover and keyboard. A file that only passes data and strings does not need `'use client'` itself.

props.text: Import from tally-charts/core on the server

props.markdown: Server code that needs a helper rather than a component should import from `tally-charts/core`. It has no React in it and is safe on the server: the formatters (`fmt`, `createFormatter`, `createFormatters`, `createDateFormatter`), `thresholds`, `heatmapLevel`, `runwayForecast`, `toNumber`, `toTime` and the shared types. The example above calls `thresholds` there to build the bins of its `ZoneMeter`. See [Formatting](/docs/formatting) and [Thresholds](/docs/thresholds) for the helpers themselves.

Props must be serializable. Strings, numbers, booleans, arrays and plain objects are, so presets such as `format="currency-compact"`, `format={{ preset: 'number', digits: 1 }}`, `data` and `x="month"` work from a server file. Function props do not: `fill`, `tone`, a function `format`, `xAxisFormat`, `tooltip` and the result of `thresholds()`, which carries methods. Pass those from a client component.

`ZoneMeter` has a way around it. Its `zones` also takes the plain part of a `thresholds()` result, so `zones={{ bins: lcp.bins, inclusive: lcp.inclusive }}` works from a Server Component, as in the example above.

**Passing a function from a server file fails when the page renders.** Next.js reports that functions cannot be passed to Client Components. Move the chart, with its function props, into a file that starts with `'use client'`.
Put the chart that needs a function in its own file with `'use client'` and import it from the server page. The page then passes only data.

`toneBy={bands}` and the function `format` stay inside the client file, where they never have to be serialized. `page.tsx` loads the data on the server and hands the array over. For dates, give the chart ISO strings and keep the default `zone` of `'utc'`, so the server and the browser draw the same ticks; see [Time scales](/docs/time-scales).
